14.text: The most important of the transformations is, however, the change of

15.text: sex. The “soft man” begins to feel like a woman. He seeks to win the

16.text: good graces of men, and succeeds easily with the aid of “spirits.” Thus he

17.text: has all the young men he could wish for striving to obtain his favor. From

18.text: these he chooses his lover, and after a time takes a husband. The marriage

19.text: is performed with the usual rites, and I must say that it forms a quite solid

20.text: union, which often lasts till the death of one of the parties. The couple

21.text: live much in the same way as do other people. The man tends his herd

22.text: and goes hunting and fishing, while the “wife” takes care of the house,

23.text: performing all domestic pursuits and work. They cohabit in a perverse

24.text: way, modo Socratis, in which the transformed wife always plays the passive
